source.title: LLM Unlearning using Gradient Ratio-Based Influence Estimation and Noise Injection

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table layouts are flattened, but the WMDP result tables support the model, method, and metric assignments used below.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether unlearning reduces targeted-knowledge accuracy while preserving general performance, a component of version A, using its own weight-selection and noise-injection framework and WMDP/MMLU accuracy. It does not test post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The WMDP accuracy results bear on whether targeted knowledge accuracy falls while retain performance is maintained. The paper reports no fine-tuning recovery attack, activation-direction ablation, quantization attack, or prompting-only recovery test. TOFU and SafePKU results concern other unlearning benchmarks and are not included as direct measures of the WMDP knowledge-accuracy endpoint. Methods mentioned only as related work or in references are not treated as tested results.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper proposing GRIN, a weight-selection and noise-injection add-on to NPO, Grad-Diff and PO. Its WMDP-Cyber and MMLU results compare its own method's forget and retain accuracy against other weight-selection baselines on Zephyr-7B-Beta (Tables 2 and 5). It runs no relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting attack, so it cannot show whether unlearning is shallow or robust. GRIN makes no claim to resist such attacks (F). The accuracy-drop-with-utility numbers are the standard unlearning evaluation that the claim takes as its starting point, not a test of it. The authors read near-chance accuracy as removal without testing that.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that GRIN gives strong forgetting with preserved utility on TOFU, WMDP and SafePKU. They call the 0.26 WMDP-Cyber accuracy with NPO near-random and read it as "effective removal of targeted information", inferring removal from accuracy alone. With Grad-Diff (Table 5), GRIN ties full fine-tuning (0.252 forget, 0.58 retain) rather than beating it, although the text says it performs best. They run no recovery attacks and draw no conclusion about robustness.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes gradient-ratio weight selection and selective noise injection followed by PO, NPO, or Grad-Diff unlearning. It does not reproduce the recovery attacks or the original methods named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by unlearning algorithm and weight-selection method; the WMDP tables compare NPO and Grad-Diff. The paper also reports that the optimal selected-weight ratio varies across tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: With Grad-Diff on Zephyr-7B-Beta, updating only the last layers leaves WMDP-Cyber accuracy at 0.45 and MMLU at 0.585, both identical to the model before unlearning. LoRA gives 0.43/0.58. Full fine-tuning, GRI, GRIN and random masks reach 0.252-0.261 (Table 5). The TOFU tables (6-7) also show LoRA and last-layer runs at or near the original model's values. Because the numbers are identical, these restricted runs may have barely changed the model under the shared hyperparameter grid, so this could be a setup artefact rather than a property of the methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-restricted unlearning (last layers only, LoRA) can fail to reduce hazardous-knowledge accuracy at all, even before any attack.

fits_no_version.finding: On TOFU (tofu-ft-llama2-7b, 10% forget) with PO, which trains refusal answers, the eight non-LoRA/Wanda variants cut forget-set keyword accuracy in generations to 0.015-0.036 and ROUGE-L to 0.072-0.114. Keyword Confidence, defined as exp(-cross-entropy) on the ground-truth answer keywords, stays at 0.90-0.965 vs 0.971 before (GRIN 0.948; Table 1). Under NPO, the same confidence does fall (full FT 0.003, GRIN 0.47; Table 7). Table 1's layout is flattened, so this column reading is ours. The paper does not discuss the gap and runs no recovery test. No row records it, because rows_left_out excludes non-WMDP results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-target unlearning removes forgotten facts from generated answers, but the model's likelihood of the forgotten answer keywords stays near its original level.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are run, so the paper cannot establish whether the reported near-chance performance survives attacks or whether knowledge was removed rather than hidden. WMDP uncertainty estimates are not reported; the appendix says experiments were repeated three times and averages were used, without reporting dispersion for these table values.
record.rows_left_out: No WMDP rows were left out. Other benchmark results were not included because they do not report the WMDP targeted-knowledge accuracy endpoint used for version A.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. The reported forget/retain accuracies are a method benchmark, not a test of the claim.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of hiding vs deleting. The paper cites Du et al. 'Textual Unlearning Gives a False Sense of Unlearning' only in related work.
No quantization. All runs are FP16, although the paper cites the quantization-failure paper (arXiv:2410.16454) as evidence of incomplete forgetting.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attacks. TOFU truth ratio uses paraphrased answers as a standard metric, not as a recovery attack.
GRIN is not evaluated against any recovery attack and claims no robustness.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) The earlier r3 item covered r4-r18 and r21-r36 by description. I expanded it into one row_fixes item per row. All 36 rows now carry versions ["none"], replacing the record's undeclared 'V1' (merge rules 1 and 5). The reason is what the rows measure: forget/retain accuracy in the paper's own method benchmark, with no recovery attack.
(2) All row states are now cannot_determine. Earlier, r3 was 'partial', and the reader's states were absent/partial/observed. With no version linked, no version effect can be read. Also, 0.282 (r3) is near the 0.25 chance level, which the catalog calls near chance for RMU's 28.2%. Each problem text gives the value against baseline and chance.
(3) In the first fits_no_version entry, I added r34 and r36. I also added the caveat that last-layer/LoRA runs match the no-unlearning numbers here and in TOFU Tables 6-7, which may be a setup artefact.
(4) I added a second fits_no_version entry on TOFU Keyword Confidence staying near its original level under PO while generation-level recall falls. This suggests output suppression, but the authors do not analyse it, so it is not counted as a test of C.
(5) In authors_conclusion, I noted the Table 5 tie and that removal is inferred from accuracy alone.
(6) The untested entries for C, D and E now note what the paper cites or uses but does not test.
Kept as before: relation uses_without_test, tranche T4, test_reason in substance, empty labels (the reader's supports/limits_scope on A stay dropped) and empty missing.
Other observations: the text points the Grad-Diff WMDP results to Tables 10-11, but they are in Table 5. Results are averages of 3 runs with no dispersion reported. Learning rate, epochs and noise variance were grid-searched per setting. The paper is a preprint carrying an AAAI 2026 copyright line. The study text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests reduction of targeted WMDP accuracy and preservation of MMLU accuracy, but does not test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
No post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or test of blocking access versus deleting knowledge.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
GRIN is evaluated for unlearning effectiveness, not for resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GRIN on Zephyr-7B-Beta with NPO and with Grad-Diff on WMDP-Cyber/MMLU
reader_labels.reason: GRIN yields WMDP-Cyber accuracy of 0.26 with NPO and 0.252 with Grad-Diff while MMLU accuracy is 0.577 and 0.58, respectively (r17–r18, r23–r24); this supports the tested unlearning-and-utility portion, not the untested attack-resistance portion.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Other tested weight-selection and fine-tuning settings in Tables 2 and 5
reader_labels.reason: Some configurations leave higher WMDP accuracy, including 0.34 for random-mask NPO and 0.43 for LoRA with Grad-Diff; last-layers-only Grad-Diff leaves accuracy at 0.45 (r9, r33, r35).
